parsed.study_design: Mixed-methods comparative case study and climate risk and vulnerability assessment
parsed.population_and_sample: Residents, municipal officials, and other stakeholders in HaSinari, Limpopo, and Prince Albert Municipality, Western Cape; eight semi-structured interviews in Prince Albert and more than 80 HaSinari residents interviewed repeatedly, supplemented by observations, surveys, focus groups, participatory activities, and documentary data.
parsed.exposure: Municipal capacity and infrastructure failures, fragmented governance and policy oversight, historically unequal service allocation, community water-management arrangements, and climate-related administrative and supply-chain vulnerabilities.
parsed.outcome: Access, reliability, affordability, availability, and equity of household/community water and sanitation services, including water-supply interruptions, dry communal taps, sanitation provision, and community-funded water delivery.
parsed.rationale: The Materials and Methods section (pp. 5–7) identifies two case studies and describes primary interviews, participant observation, surveys, focus groups, documentary review, and thematic analysis. Results sections 3.2 and 4.1–4.4 (pp. 10–15) empirically connect municipal failure, unequal allocation, fragmented oversight, and community water committees to WASH access, reliability, affordability, and exclusion in the two study populations.
